title: Working with AI (process)
_note: Move: process-criteria; Edge E5. Add to the rubric of the designated AI activity. Grades the quality of engagement, not the product. Pick the criteria that match the activity; keep the total small (about 20-30% of the assignment). Rewrite descriptions in the course's own terms. Grading time: about 3 minutes per submission for all four.

criteria.long_description: A dated prediction and the student's own framing (including the constraint or value that matters here) exist before the AI output, and were not rewritten after it.

ratings.long_description: Prediction and framing are specific and come first
Present but generic, or partly after the fact
No framing before the AI output

criteria.long_description: For the claims that matter, a verdict, a target and a mechanism are written before any lookup. A correct verdict with no mechanism earns partial credit.

ratings.long_description: Verdict, target and mechanism for each important claim
Verdicts without mechanisms, or only some claims
A general impression with no specific claims

criteria.long_description: Claims were checked against evidence independent of the AI (hand calculation, primary source, data, test). Another AI agreeing does not count. What was not checked is stated.

ratings.long_description: Independent checks, results recorded, unchecked items named
Some independent checks; gaps not named
Checked only with the same or another AI

criteria.long_description: Says what was kept from the AI, what was rejected or overridden and why, and what the student added. Disclosure is honest and specific. Heavy AI use that is honestly disclosed can earn full credit.

ratings.long_description: Decisions and reasons are specific and traceable
Disclosure present but generic ("used AI to help")
